newsitem.title: GERMANY: Chinese feeds output seen rising fast - Toepfer.
newsitem.headline: Chinese feeds output seen rising fast - Toepfer.

text.p: Compound feed output in China may rise to 75-80 million tonnes by the year 2000 from 56 million in 96/97 and 52.5 million in 95/96, according to grain trader Alfred C Toepfer.
Citing population and income growth along with limited domestic raw materials, it saw chances for foreign maize and oilmeals suppliers to win exports to China.

China would import 3.5 million tonnes of oilmeals in 96/97, more than twice the 1.6 million seen in 95/96, Toepfer said in its monthly market report. This was mostly soymeal, but fishmeal also featured highly.
Imports of soymeal alone in 97/98 were forecast at four million tonnes and those of fishmeal at one million.
China's compound feed production has risen by an average nine percent over the last five years, making the country the largest single producer after the United States.
Toepfer said some 50 percent of production was poultry feed while 40 percent was pig feed and the remaining 10 percent dairy cow feed.
Grain inclusion rates were not precisely known but estimated at 70-75 percent. The 96/97 tonnage of grain used in compound feed was estimated at 40 million tonnes.

China's total grain consumption in animal feed (mostly on-farm) was estimated at 120 million tonnes by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, Toepfer said. This was 46 percent of total domestic grain output.
An estimated two thirds of the 120 million tonnes were maize.
The USDA forecast China's per-capita meat consumption at 60 kilos in 2005 after 47 kilos in 1996, Toepfer said.
The 47 kilos were broken down into 33 kilos of pork, 10 kilos of poultry and four kilos of beef.
EU consumers currently eat an average 43 kilos of pork and 21 kilos of poultry per annum.
